entities.summary: John Thomas Dunlop was an American administrator, labor economist, and educator. Dunlop was the United States Secretary of Labor between 1975 and 1976 under President Gerald Ford. He was Director of the United States Cost of Living Council from 1973 to 1974, Chairman of the United States Commission on the Future of Worker-Management Relations from 1993 to 1995, which produced the Dunlop Report in 1994. He was also arbitrator and impartial chairman of various United States labor-management committees, and a member of numerous government boards on industrial relations disputes and economic stabilization.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As Director of the United States Cost of Living Council and Chairman of the United States Commission on the Future of Worker-Management Relations, Dunlop's work influenced labor policies and industrial relations in North America. His report, the Dunlop Report, shaped the future of worker-management relations.
